title: GFCC Invitation Federation Contract v1
description: Federated invitation lifecycle. An invitation grants eligibility for one declared audience and purpose; it is not a user identity, an authentication credential, or a device credential.
non_goals: a device identity or device proof
a PlanetX fleet invite unless that audience explicitly owns the invitation

external_subject.notes: External account identifiers (including Supabase Auth UUIDs) are namespaced by issuer and mapped to canonical principal.sub by the trusted identity authority. A client-supplied UUID is never authoritative.

identity.issuer_binding: The trusted service derives the namespaced external identity from its verified session and attaches canonical_sub only when the identity authority has established that mapping; it does not trust caller-provided identifiers.
identity.redeemer_binding: The trusted service derives the namespaced external identity from the verified redeemer session and resolves canonical_sub through the identity authority when a mapping exists.

id.description: Stable opaque identifier for internal reference; it is not a bearer secret. Do not encode identity or authorization claims in it.

audience.description: The single service/product boundary allowed to validate and redeem this invitation, e.g. genzer.terminal.registration or gfcc.circle.

purpose.description: The specific action granted within the audience, e.g. account_registration or circle_admission. Purpose is not inferred from a query parameter.

recipient.description: Optional recipient restriction. When absent, any otherwise eligible authenticated principal may redeem.

extensions.description: Audience-specific non-authoritative metadata. It must not override identity, audience, purpose, expiry, or redemption policy.

idempotency_key.description: Audience-scoped retry key. Repeating the same successful redemption by the same principal returns the original outcome and does not consume another redemption.

principal_binding.description: Opaque server-side binding to the verified authenticated principal. Do not use a client-supplied UUID.

credential_id.description: Identifier for lookup only; it is not proof of device possession.

proof.description: Opaque device response verified by the device credential authority. Algorithm, encoding, and hardware-attestation profile are intentionally deferred until the wearable is specified.

issue.notes: The issuing service derives the issuer principal from its verified session. The caller cannot select issuer sub, audience, or purpose outside its authorized policy.

inspect.notes: Any pre-authentication preview is limited to generic validity guidance and must not expose issuer identity or private account data.

prepare_redemption.notes: Verify the caller session and derive its namespaced external identity; resolve canonical principal.sub when an identity mapping exists. If device_policy.mode is registered_credential_required, issue a short-lived single-use challenge bound to invitation, audience, purpose, and authenticated principal. Do not redeem yet.

redeem.device_proof: required only when invitation.device_policy.mode is registered_credential_required
atomic_checks: invitation exists and belongs to the requested audience and purpose
invitation is active, unexpired, and below max_redemptions
recipient restriction matches the verified principal when present
device proof is valid when required and the challenge is unused and unexpired
redemption is recorded against the verified redeemer principal
redeem.notes: Consume the invitation and record redemption in one atomic operation. Never mint or exchange a session for the issuer's subject. An invitation only grants its declared eligibility; authentication remains the redeemer's own session.

revoke.notes: The issuer may revoke an unredeemed invitation within policy. Revocation and redemption must serialize so only one terminal state wins.

device_policy.future_wearable: registered_credential_required may be selected after device enrollment and proof requirements are specified.
device_policy.failure: If device proof is required and unavailable or invalid, redemption fails closed; the service must not silently downgrade the policy.
device_policy.uuid_rule: A device UUID or credential_id is a lookup hint only. Device authentication requires verification of a challenge-bound proof from a registered credential.

terminal_invite.value: Short-lived, single-use opaque handoff handle. It is not a Supabase UUID, raw reusable invite code, or login credential.
flow: Open the public landing page with the opaque handle.
Authenticate the redeemer with the terminal identity provider.
POST the handle over TLS to the terminal invitation authority.
Verify the authenticated session, resolve its namespaced subject, then atomically redeem.
security: Possession of the handoff handle alone grants no session or account access.
Do not place raw reusable invitation secrets, user UUIDs, or device identifiers in URLs.
Redact handoff handles from access logs, analytics, and referrer propagation.

terminal_invite.meaning: Invitation handle for the Genzer Terminal registration audience.
terminal_invite.transport_value: Short-lived opaque handoff handle as defined in transport.terminal_invite.
terminal_invite.may_be_forwarded_by_planetx: Only as opaque data when the product's cross-product transfer policy explicitly allows it; PlanetX must not validate, redeem, or reinterpret it. Never place it in the legacy PlanetX join parameter.

fleet_invite.rule: Must not be interpreted as terminal_invite.

ref.rule: Must never authorize, authenticate, identify a principal, or substitute for either invitation.

region.rule: Must never affect authentication, identity mapping, device verification, or invitation eligibility.

invariants: Canonical GFCC identity is principal.sub; external identities are namespaced by issuer and mapped by a trusted identity authority.
Client-supplied user UUIDs, device UUIDs, ref values, and invitation handles are not authentication proof.
An invitation is scoped to exactly one audience and purpose; codes from different invitation authorities are never interchangeable.
The authenticated redeemer is derived from a verified session and is the subject recorded by redemption.
Invitation validation/preview does not consume an invitation; successful redemption is atomic and retry-safe.
Device proof is independent from user authentication and invitation eligibility.
Current PWA flows do not claim hardware-backed or wearable-device authentication.
Legacy circle redemption that issues a session for the invitation issuer is not conformant to this contract and must not be used as a cross-product registration flow.

migration.legacy_circle_redeem: The existing GFCC circle redemption implementation issues a session for the invitation-bound subject. It is legacy behavior and is not conformant to this contract's authenticated-redeemer binding. Migrating that flow requires a separate implementation change and rollout plan.

issuer.description: Trusted identity provider identifier, e.g. the configured Supabase Auth issuer.

subject.description: Subject obtained from a verified provider session, never trusted from a request body.

canonical_sub.description: Trusted identity-authority mapping to GFCC principal.sub, when established.

credential_id.description: Audit reference only; not a device proof.

assurance_profile.description: Optional verifier-defined assurance label. Values are deferred until the wearable and trust chain are specified.
